benchmark_details.name: Nursing Staff Duty Rosters
benchmark_details.overview: Evaluates models' ability to extract structured schedule data from an icon-based nursing staff duty roster of a Swiss care facility, April 2025: shift types, half-day splits, alternate unit assignments and staff metadata.

purpose_and_intended_users.goal: Measure how well vision-language models read a dense, icon-based staff planning grid: mapping each cell to its date via a separate header, identifying shift icons via a separate legend, and recording half-day splits, shading and alternate unit assignments as structured records. The results are meant to guide nursing and health services researchers who need staffing data from planning sheets that exist only as printouts or scans.
tasks: date alignment of cells across separate images
purpose_and_intended_users.limitations: 21 rows from one monthly roster of one ward in one facility; results do not transfer automatically to other roster software, layouts or icon sets. Days and shifts are compared by position, so a model that omits a day or splits a cell differently shifts every later field into a mismatch. All fields count equally, so each row's 30 dates and roughly 31 shifts of four fields each outweigh the four person fields and the year and month. The legend holds 33 icons, of which the ground truth uses 20; `Freier Tag` alone makes up a third of all shifts.
out_of_scope_uses: drawing conclusions about the staff, the ward or the facility
re-identifying staff members or analysing their absences
evaluating general table or handwriting recognition

data.source: One monthly staff planning sheet (PEP, file `04-25_PEP_02-12-01`) for April 2025 from one ward of a Swiss nursing care facility, provided by Ana-Maria Leonte and Franziska Zúñiga through the INTERSCALE study of the Institute of Nursing Science, University of Basel (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06473051). The facility is not named. The sheet was segmented by hand into one image per staff member's row; the roster header (dates and weekdays) and the icon legend are separate images.
data.annotation: Maximilian Hindermann (annotator) created the ground truth by hand, with Ana-Maria Leonte and Franziska Zúñiga as domain experts, following the extraction rules in the [prompt file](prompts/prompt.txt).
data.collection_date: Source documents: April 2025. Added to the benchmark: April 2026.
data.contamination_controls: None. The images, prompt and ground truth have been public in this repository since April 2026.

methods: zero-shot structured extraction; each request carries the header image, the legend image and one roster row
structured JSON output requested using the `Schedule` dataclass, with `icon` restricted to the 33 legend names
benchmark default output cap of 98,304 tokens; a test rule can override it and model-specific ceilings can lower it
methodology.calculation:
Every terminal field present in the response or the ground truth (for example `persons[0].days[4].shifts[0].icon`) is compared at the same path; empty strings count as missing. Values are compared with a rapidfuzz similarity score on their string form, and a field is a match at a score of 0.92 or above.

- TP: both have a value and the score is at least 0.92
- FP and FN: both have a value but the score is below 0.92 (the field counts once as each)
- FP: only the response has a value
- FN: only the ground truth has a value

A `null` icon or alternate unit on both sides counts as nothing. F1 micro sums TP, FP and FN over all rows before computing F1; F1 macro averages the per-row F1 values, each rounded to two decimals. There are no configurable field-selection rules. A response that does not parse as JSON is skipped rather than scored as zero, so both aggregates cover only scored rows.
methodology.interpretation: Scores range from 0 to 1; higher is better. Both metrics are dominated by shift-level fields; a low score can come from misaligned dates as much as from misread icons.
methodology.baseline_results:
Model results are available on the [benchmark page](https://rise-services.rise.unibas.ch/benchmarks/p/benchmarks/duty_rosters) and in `results/<date>/<test_id>/` at the repository root. Compare runs with the same prompt, scoring rules and ground-truth revision, and report the number of successfully scored objects alongside the score. There is no fixed model baseline with a run ID and date.

Observed across models: mapping cells to dates across the separate header image is the largest source of error. Models also confuse empty cells with `Freier Tag` or assign icons such as `HomeOffice` to them.
methodology.validation: The ground truth was created by a single annotator, Maximilian Hindermann; no second check is recorded. Scoring is deterministic; the scorer has no dedicated test.
methodology.validity_justification: Field-level F1 reflects the downstream use: each shift becomes a record in a staffing dataset, so a field is either usable or needs correction.

ethical_and_legal_considerations.privacy_and_anonymity: The roster is from April 2025 and covers living people. It was anonymised by the facility before release: neither the images nor the ground truth contain names, staff are identified only by the IDs the INTERSCALE study assigned (the handwritten numbers in the margin), the facility is not named, and the ward label is cropped from the header image. Each row records a profession group, employment percentage and a month of shifts and absences, including sick days (two rows) and a month of maternity protection (one row).
ethical_and_legal_considerations.consent_procedures: The facility released the anonymised roster for publication through the INTERSCALE study.
ethical_and_legal_considerations.compliance_with_regulations: As the roster is anonymised and carries only study IDs (see Privacy and Anonymity), it contains no personal data that identifies staff. The facility granted its use under CC BY 4.0 through the INTERSCALE study. No separate reuse terms are stated for the ground truth. No separate ethical review was carried out for the benchmark.
